questions.question: How many positive factors of 76 are there?
questions.solution:
76

= 1 × 76

= 2 × 38

= 4 × 19

∴ Number of positive factors of 76 are 6.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are true?

I. 2⁶⁰⁰ > 7⁹⁰⁰

II. 3⁴⁰⁰ > 9⁵⁰⁰
questions.solution:
We know that,

3² > 2² (i.e. 9 > 4)

Also, 3³ > 2³ (i.e. 27 > 8)

**The above equations imply that if L.H.S has a number and power both greater than the number and power of the R.H.S then L.H.S is always greater than R.H.S. **

But in the given statements we find that in both the statements L.H.S has the lesser number and lesser power than R.H.S.

So,

2⁶⁰⁰ < 7⁹⁰⁰

3⁴⁰⁰ < 9⁵⁰⁰

∴ Neither of the statements is true

questions.question: How many numbers are there between 200 and 285 which are divisible by 7?

questions.question: If N = √9 + √7, then what is the value of (1/N)?
questions.solution:
Given,

N = √9 + √7

(1/N) = 1/(√9 + √7)

Rationalizing the denominator by multiplying and dividing by (√9 – √7)

= (√9 – √7)/ [(√9 + √7) (√9 – √7)]

(∵ (a + b)(a – b) = a² – b²)

= (√9 – √7)/(9 – 7)

= (√9 – √7)/2

∴ (1/N) = (√9 – √7)/2

questions.question: What is the unit’s digit of 216²¹⁶?
questions.solution:
In order to find the unit’s digit of 216²¹⁶, we should find the unit’s digit of 6²¹⁶

We know that,

Cyclicity of the number 6 is 1 i.e.,

6¹ = __6__

6² = 3__6__

6³ = 21__6__

6⁴ = 129__6__

⇒ Unit’s digit of 6⁴×⁵⁴ is 6

∴ The unit’s digit of 216²¹⁶ = 6

questions.question: P, Q and R undertook a work for Rs. 52000. Together P and Q complete (2/5)th part of the work. What is the share (in Rs) of R?
questions.solution:

questions.question: If the area of an equilateral triangle is 12√3 m², then what is the value (in metres) of its height?
questions.solution:
We know that,

Area of an equilateral triangle of side ‘a’ = √3a²/4

⇒ 12√3 = √3a²/4

⇒ a² = 48

⇒ a = 4√3 m

We know that,

Height of an equilateral triangle = √3a/2

⇒ Height of the equilateral triangle = (√3 × 4√3)/2 = 6 m

∴ Height of the equilateral triangle = 6 m

questions.question: A trader gives a discount of 20% on the marked price. To earn profit of 12%, by how much percent should he mark the price of his goods higher than its cost price?
questions.solution:
Let the cost price (CP) be Rs. 100.

**Formula: **Selling price (SP) = Cost price (CP) + Profit

⇒ SP of goods = CP of goods + Profit

⇒ SP of goods = 100 + 12 = Rs. 112

Formula: Marked price (MP) = SP + Discount

⇒ MP of goods = 112 + (20% of MP of goods)

⇒ MP of goods = 112/0.8 = Rs. 140

∴ % by which the trader has to mark his goods higher than its cost price = [(140 – 100)/100] × 100 = 40%

questions.question: An article has marked price of Rs 7200 and is available at a discount of 20%. The shopkeeper gives another discount to the buyer and sells the article for Rs 4896. What is the second discount (in %) offered?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Marked price (MP) of the article = Rs. 7200

First Discount = 20%

**Formula used:**

Discount = MP - SP

Discount % = (Discount/MP) × 100

**Calculation:**

Marked price (MP) of the article = Rs. 7200

Price after a discount of 20% = 7200 – (20% of 7200) = Rs. 5760

Let the second discount offered be ‘x%’.

⇒ Price after a second discount of x% = Rs. 4896

⇒ 5760 – (x% of 5760) = 4896

⇒ (x/100) × 5760 = 864

⇒ x = (864 × 100)/5760 = 15%

∴ Second discount offered = 15%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Discount = 20% (1/5)

Let,

MP = 5

SP = 5 - 1 = 4

⇒ 5 = 7200 (Actual MP)

⇒ 1 = 1440

SP = 4 × 1440 = Rs. 5760

Final SP = Rs. 4896

Discount % = (Discount/MP) × 100

Discount = 5760 - 4896 = Rs. 864

Discount % = (864/5760) × 100

⇒ 15 %

questions.question: If M : N = 2 : 7 and M : O = 4 : 3, then what is (M + N) : (N + O)?
If the sum of two numbers is equal to five times of their difference, then what is the ratio of the numbers?
questions.solution:
Let the two numbers be ‘x’ and ‘y’ respectively.

According to the question,

(x + y) = 5(x – y)

⇒ y + 5y = 5x – x

⇒ 6y = 4x

⇒ x/y = 6/4 = 3/2

∴ The ratio of the numbers = 3 ∶ 2

questions.question: Average of 15 numbers is 20. If a number 4 is also included, then what will be the average of these 16 numbers?
questions.solution:
**Calculation**:

Average of 15 numbers = 20

Sum of 15 numbers = 20 × 15 = 300

Sum of 16 numbers where 4 is the 16th number = 300 + 4 = 304

⇒ Average of these 16 numbers = 304/16 = 19

∴ Average of these 16 numbers = 19

questions.question: Sahil sold a fan to Ankit at a profit of 10%. Ankit sold the fan to Pulkit at a profit of 20%. If Pulkit pays Rs 330 for fan, then for how much (in Rs) Sahil bought the fan?
questions.solution:
Let the cost price (CP) of the fan for which Sahil bought be Rs. x.

We know that,

**Selling price (SP) = CP + Profit**

SP of the fan to Ankit = x + (10% of x) = Rs. 1.1x

SP of the fan to Pulkit = 1.1x + (20% of x) = Rs. 1.32x

⇒ 330 = 1.32x

⇒ x = 330/1.32 = Rs. 250

∴ CP of the fan for which Sahil bought = Rs. 250

questions.question: On selling an article for Rs 455, a shopkeeper losses 30%. For how much (in Rs) he should sell the article in order to earn a profit of 30%?
questions.solution:
**Short trick∶**

Required value = 455 × 1.3/0.7 = Rs. 845

**Detailed solution∶**

Selling price (SP) of the article = Rs. 455

We know that,

⇒ SP of the article = CP of the article - Loss

⇒ 455 = CP of the article – (30% of CP of the article)

⇒ CP of the article = 455/0.7 = Rs. 650

We know that,

**SP = CP + Profit**

⇒ SP of the article if profit is 30% = 650 + (30% of 650)

⇒ SP of the article = 650 + 195 = Rs. 845

∴ SP of the article = Rs. 845

questions.question: A man saves 36% of his income in 9 months. If he wants to save the same amount in 6 months, then by how much percentage should he increase his monthly savings?
questions.solution:
We know that,

**Income = Expenditure + Savings**

Let income in 9 months be Rs. 100

⇒ Savings in 9 months = 36% of 100 = Rs. 36

Savings in 6 months = 6 × (36/9) = Rs. 24

∴ Required % = [(36 – 24)/24] × 100 = 50%

questions.question: Two numbers are 25% and 15% less than the third number respectively. First number is what percent less than the second number?
questions.solution:
Let the third number be ‘x’.

First number = x – (25% of x) = 0.75x

Second number = x – (15% of x) = 0.85x

∴ Required % = [(0.85x – 0.75x)/0.85x] × 100 = 11.76%

questions.question: A car travels at a speed of 75 m/s for 2 hours. What is the distance (in km) travelled by the car?
questions.solution:
Given,

Speed of the car = 75 m/s = 75 × (18/5) = 270 km/hr (∵ **1 m/s = (18/5) km/hr**)

We know that,

**Distance = Speed × Time**

⇒ Distance travelled by the car in 2 hours = 270 × 2 = 540 km

∴ Distance travelled by the car in 2 hours = 540 km

questions.question: An 800 meters long train crosses a 450 meter long bridge in 50 seconds. What is speed (in km/hr) of the train?
questions.solution:
We know that,

Speed = Distance/Time

⇒ Speed of the train = (800 + 450)/50 = 1250/50 = 25 m/s = 25 × (18/5) = 90 km/hr

(∵ 1 m/s = (18/5) km/hr)

∴ Speed of the train = 90 km/hr

questions.question: What is the simple interest (in Rs) on a principal of Rs 2000 at the rate of 5% per annum for 2 years?
questions.solution:
We know the formula for simple interest-

SI = (P × T × R)/100

Where,

SI = Simple interest

P = Principal

R = Rate of interest

T = Time period

⇒ SI = (2000 × 2 × 5)/100 = Rs. 200

∴ Simple interest = Rs. 200
